body:
m1 - REBASED SHA, because main moved under the candidate while it was waiting. GATE 19510e9, NOT d9d7d97. Base is now 1e8da51.

WHY I REBASED RATHER THAN LEAVING IT: e4bbf5b landed two tolerance constants in hsmm.scala and Resolution.scala. hsmm is on my change's path, so a merged tree would not have been the tree I gated. You gate merged trees, and I would rather hand you one that exists than one that did.

RE-VERIFIED ON THE NEW BASE, not carried over:
  align 200/200, fixtures 116/116
  GOLDEN CHECKSUM UNCHANGED: 32f509c93358ae7d8748c5d7f940c4ff69db33ceac78eb61073ec0dff43bab2f
  at 25,960 bytes, byte-identical to what I posted.

That last line is the one worth noting: the tolerance constants did not move the encoded artifact at all, so the key-count reconciliation I gave you still holds exactly - 666 bytes, 18 supportWeight keys, 37 bytes each, values 0x3ff0000000000000 on ten cells and 0x3fee9131abf0b767 on eight.

Everything else in my previous message stands unchanged. Content is identical; only the base moved.

This is the third time today I have rebased and re-derived rather than assumed composition held - twice against the scout's landings and now against yours. All three times the numbers were unchanged, which is a decent argument that the estimand work is genuinely modular, but I would not have been able to say so without checking each time.
